# Add idempotent Pages environment setup script

## Summary

Adds a reproducible, executable `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` that adds the `tag:v*` deployment policy to the `github-pages` environment via `gh api`, only when it is missing, and never removes the existing `dev` branch policy. Ships with automated tests (test-first inside the item).

## User story

As a future maintainer, I want a documented, idempotent script that configures the `github-pages` environment deployment policy, so I do not have to rediscover the `dev`-only policy failure that blocked every `v*` release tag.

## Context

- Parent acceptance criterion **AC2** requires `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` to exist, be executable, add the `v*` tag policy only when missing, be safe to re-run (second run makes no change, exits 0), and fail loudly when `gh` is missing or unauthenticated.
- There is currently **no** `scripts/` directory in the repository.
- The live environment already has exactly one policy: `branch:dev`. The script must preserve it.

## Scope

In scope:

- The setup script and its hermetic tests.

Out of scope:

- Applying the policy to the live repository (see *Apply tag policy and verify deploy*), and README documentation (see *Document Pages environment policy*).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` exists, is executable, adds the `v*` tag policy only when missing, and is safe to re-run (second run makes no change and exits 0).
- The script preserves the existing `dev` branch policy and adds only a `tag:v*` policy (never deletes or rewrites existing policies).
- It fails loudly with a clear, actionable message when `gh` is missing or unauthenticated (non-zero exit, no partial writes).
- Automated tests cover add-once, idempotent second run, dev-policy preservation, and fail-loud-without-`gh`/auth, using a stubbed `gh` on `PATH` (no live API calls).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`bash -n` syntax check, `npm test`, and `npm run build` all pass).

## Minimal Implementation

- Script: accept an optional `--repo <owner/name>` (default: resolve from the current clone via `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`). Preflight `command -v gh` and `gh auth status`; exit non-zero with an actionable message otherwise.
- Read existing policies with `gh api repos/$REPO/environments/github-pages/deployment-branch-policies`; if a policy with `type == "tag"` and `name == "v*"` is present, print "already configured" and exit 0 without any write.
- Otherwise `POST` `{"name":"v*","type":"tag"}` to the same endpoint, then `GET` again to verify the policy is present (fail loudly if verification fails).
- Tests: create a temp `gh` stub executable that logs argv and returns canned JSON, prepend its directory to `PATH`, run the script with `bash`, and assert the recorded calls (no POST on second run; POST payload on first run; `dev` never deleted) plus exit codes. Keep all tests hermetic.

## Deliverables

- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` (executable).
- Hermetic script tests wired into `npm test`.
- Green `npm test` / `npm run build`.

## Dependencies

None (sequenced after *Add Pages deploy trigger regression test*).

## Key Files

- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` — New idempotent script that adds/verifies the `v*` tag deployment policy on the `github-pages` environment via `gh api`.
- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.test.ts` — New hermetic tests using a stubbed `gh`.
- `vitest.config.ts` — Test include globs; may need to cover `scripts/`.
data.title: Add idempotent Pages environment setup script

# Apply tag policy and verify deploy

## Summary

Applies the `tag:v*` deployment policy to the live `github-pages` environment using the setup script, then verifies the release Pages deploy end to end (policy present, `deploy` job succeeds, Pages URL serves the game).

## User story

As a release runner, I want pushing a `v*` release tag to deploy to GitHub Pages without environment-protection rejection, so that the release PR's checks pass and the ship wrapper merges the PR automatically; and as a player, I want every release published automatically at the project Pages URL.

## Context

- Parent acceptance criteria **AC1** (tag policy present) and **AC3** (deploy succeeds end to end) are verified by this item.
- Evidence of the current failure: workflow run `35993333739` (`event: push`, `headBranch: v0.1.5`) — `build` succeeded, `deploy` failed with zero steps due to environment protection.
- The active `gh` token has `repo` scope and the repository reports `admin: true`, so the script can apply the policy directly; if the token lacks admin the operator applies it manually and this item records the exact command.

## Scope

In scope:

- Running the setup script against `SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell`.
- Verifying the policy via the GitHub API.
- Re-running the failed tag workflow (or pushing a fresh `v*` tag through the normal release flow) and confirming the Pages URL serves.

Out of scope:

- Editing the workflow or the ship skill.
- Broader Pages source configuration changes (only revisit if the deploy still fails after the policy is in place).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The `github-pages` environment has a deployment policy for tags matching `v*`, in addition to the existing `dev` branch policy; `gh api repos/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell/environments/github-pages/deployment-branch-policies` outputs both `branch:dev` and `tag:v*`.
- Deploy succeeds end to end: re-running workflow run `35993333739` (tag `v0.1.5`) completes with both the `build` and `deploy` jobs `success`, and `https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/` serves the game.
- If the historical run cannot be re-run, a fresh `v*` tag is pushed through the normal release flow and its `deploy` job succeeds; the fallback taken is recorded.
- Verification evidence (API output showing both policies, workflow run conclusion, and an HTTP check of the Pages URL) is recorded as a comment on `AH-0MUFGUR9C003XD77`.

## Minimal Implementation

- Run `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` against the repository (from the *Add idempotent Pages environment setup script* item); capture its output.
- Verify with `gh api repos/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell/environments/github-pages/deployment-branch-policies --jq '.branch_policies[] | "\(.type):\(.name)"'` and confirm `branch:dev` and `tag:v*`.
- `gh run rerun 35993333739` (re-run the failed jobs) and `gh run watch 35993333739` / `gh run view 35993333739 --json conclusion,jobs`; if re-run is not permitted, push a fresh `v*` tag via the release flow and verify that run instead.
- `curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://sorratheorc.github.io/AI_Hell/` and confirm a 2xx response.
- Post a comment on the parent work item with the raw evidence.

## Deliverables

- Applied `tag:v*` environment policy (preserving `branch:dev`).
- Successful Pages deploy for the release tag.
- Evidence comment on the parent work item.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by *Add idempotent Pages environment setup script* (`wl dep add <this-id> <setup-script-id>`).

## Key Files

- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` — The script run to apply the policy.
- GitHub repository setting — `github-pages` environment deployment policy (applied by the script, verified via `gh api`).

# Document Pages environment policy

## Summary

Documents the `github-pages` environment deployment policy requirement (tag `v*` plus the existing `dev` branch) and the reproducible setup script in `README.md`, so a maintainer can recover the configuration without rediscovering the `dev`-only policy failure.

## User story

As a future maintainer, I want the Pages environment policy requirement and its setup script documented, so I can set up or recover the repository's release deploys reproducibly.

## Context

- Parent acceptance criterion **AC5** requires all related documentation to be updated, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs entries.
- `README.md` currently has no Pages/deployment configuration section. There is no `docs/dev/` or wiki entry for this in the repository.
- The script's `--help` / header comments are also part of the documentation surface.

## Scope

In scope:

- A deployment subsection in `README.md`.
- Header/usage comments in the setup script (delivered with the script item).

Out of scope:

- A separate docs site or wiki (none exists in this repository).

## Acceptance Criteria

- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- `README.md` gains a subsection documenting the `github-pages` environment deployment policy requirement (tag `v*` alongside `dev`) and the purpose of the tag-triggered deploy.
- The README documents how to run `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh`, that it is idempotent and safe to re-run, and the `gh` authentication/admin requirement (including the manual fallback `gh api` command when admin rights are unavailable).
- The documented commands match the script's actual CLI and output, verified by reading the script and running it with `--help`.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a "Deploying to GitHub Pages" (or equivalent) subsection under the existing release workflow material in `README.md`.
- State: releases publish on `v*` tag push; the `github-pages` environment must allow both `branch:dev` and `tag:v*`; run the script to apply/verify; requires a `gh` token with repository admin.
- Include the exact policy-inspection command and a note on the `dev`-only failure mode the script prevents.
- Keep the section concise and link it from the release/ship narrative where relevant.

## Deliverables

- Updated `README.md` deployment subsection.
- Consistent script header comments / usage output (delivered with the script).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by *Add idempotent Pages environment setup script* (`wl dep add <this-id> <setup-script-id>`), since the docs describe the script's real CLI.

## Key Files

- `README.md` — New deployment subsection documenting the `github-pages` environment policy requirement and script usage.
- `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.sh` — Source of truth for the documented CLI and behaviour.
